context:
Goal: a challenge to one of your past rulings reaches you only when it carries real evidence.
Problem (rule): your restart-plan ruling R39 refuses a re-ask that brings no new fact, so a re-ask with a new fact passes; the lane built it stricter, so a new fact alone is refused unless the challenge has all four parts.
Based on (read): restart-plan R39, items 1 and 4 (refuse a re-ask with no new fact).
Based on (read): the four parts come from rule outcomes-stale-decision-protocol: the record and its sentence, a measure or "unmeasured", the outcome the ruling protected, and a proposed fix.
Departs from: R39, where a re-ask with a new fact passes — the build refuses it unless all four parts are present.
Meanwhile: the merge of the lane's branch waits on this item.

options.gain: Fewer half-made challenges reach you, and the bar matches your rule for stale decisions.
options.how: A challenge passes only with all four parts, new fact or not.
options.label: Keep the four-part bar
options.lose: A real new fact without the other three parts is refused until the session writes them.

options.gain: Matches R39 exactly, and a session can bring you a new fact without writing the full four-part case.
options.how: The guard lets a re-ask through when it names a new fact.
options.label: R39 as written: a new fact alone passes (Recommended)
options.lose: Thin challenges with one fact and no proposed fix reach you.

reply: Filed: b. Yes, four parts was overkill; a challenge to a past ruling passes on a new fact alone. Lane ruling-challenge-passes builds b and its merge is no longer held.
short: Past-ruling challenge: four parts or a new fact?
title: Must a challenge to a past ruling carry all four parts, even when it brings a new fact?
why: Recommended: b. Your doubt that four parts is overkill holds; R39 already stops re-asks with no new fact.
